story: Romulus and Remus were twin brothers born in Alba Longa to Rhea Silvia, a Vestal Virgin and daughter of the deposed king Numitor. She conceived them after the god Mars visited her in a sacred grove. Fearing them as threats to his rule, King Amulius, who had overthrown Numitor, ordered the infants killed and had them abandoned on the bank of the river Tiber. The god Tiberinus saved them, and they survived thanks to a she-wolf who suckled them in a cave, the Lupercal. A shepherd named Faustulus found and raised them, and they grew up as leaders among the local shepherd community, unaware of their true heritage. As young men, they became involved in a conflict between supporters of Numitor and Amulius. Remus was captured and taken to Alba Longa, where his identity was suspected. Romulus organized a rescue, and the brothers learned of their true parentage. Joining forces with their grandfather Numitor, they overthrew and killed Amulius, restoring Numitor to the throne. The twins then set out to found their own city near the seven hills. They quarreled over which hill to build on—Romulus favoring the Palatine, Remus the Aventine—and sought divine approval through augury. Remus saw six birds, but Romulus saw twelve and claimed victory. The dispute escalated, and Remus was killed, either by Romulus or by one of his supporters, after insulting the new city. Romulus went on to found Rome, establishing its government, army, religious traditions, and institutions, ruling as its first king for many years.
blind: Two twin brothers were born in a smaller city to a woman who was a consecrated priestess and daughter of a deposed ruler. She conceived them after a war god visited her in a sacred grove. Fearing them as threats to his power, the usurping king who had overthrown her father ordered the infants killed and had them abandoned on the bank of a great river. A river god saved them, and they survived because a she-wolf suckled them in a cave. A shepherd found and raised them, and they grew up as leaders among the local herding community, unaware of their true heritage. As young men, they became involved in a conflict between supporters of their grandfather and the usurping king. One brother was captured and taken to the smaller city, where his identity was suspected. The other organized a rescue, and the brothers learned of their true parentage. Joining forces with their grandfather, they overthrew and killed the usurper, restoring the grandfather to the throne. The twins then set out to found their own city near a group of hills. They quarreled over which hill to build on, each favoring a different one, and sought divine approval through bird-omen divination. One brother saw six birds, but the other saw twelve and claimed victory. The dispute escalated, and the losing brother was killed, either by his twin or by one of the twin's supporters, after insulting the new city. The surviving brother went on to found the city, establishing its government, army, religious traditions, and institutions, ruling as its first king for many years.
